rows.separate_pay_conditions: Separate pay requires documented modifier 22, excluding E&M, and assistant modifier on non-global cesarean delivery.
Separate pay allowed for documented distinct obstetric services, assistant surgeons, and supported modifier 22 cesareans.
Pays assistant modifiers if medically necessary; CMS teaching rules apply, cesareans capped at delivery-only rate.
Assistant surgeons bill primary cesarean delivery-only codes with assistant modifier; multiple-procedure reductions apply.

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Cesarean delivery is included in the global maternity package when full obstetric care is billed. Delivery-only cesarean codes are separately reimbursable only when the global package does not apply and an appropriate assistant surgeon modifier is present.

This commercial modifier 22 policy is not a DRG-specific maternity outlier rule. It permits additional reimbursement when a cesarean requires substantially increased work, time, and complexity, including multiple births delivered by cesarean section when documented.

Commercial maternity policy treats cesarean delivery as included in the global obstetrical package. Global reimbursement is allowed once per pregnancy when antepartum, delivery, and postpartum care are all furnished by the same provider or TIN. Separate payment is limited; assistant-surgeon cesarean delivery-only services may be reimbursed when properly modifier-appended. Overlapping maternity claims may be denied or recouped.

reimbursement_policies.policy_title: Assistant-at-Surgery Policy, Professional - Reimbursement Policy - UnitedHealthcare Commercial Plans
reimbursement_policies.evidence: Commercial assistant-at-surgery policy reimburses eligible cesarean section services on professional claims. Global cesarean codes are repriced to corresponding non-global delivery codes, and only one assistant is payable per procedure when correct assistant modifiers are present.

reimbursement_policies.policy_title: Obstetrical Policy, Professional - Reimbursement Policy - UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange
reimbursement_policies.evidence: This policy addresses professional obstetrical billing and cesarean delivery CPT services on CMS-1500 claims. It does not contain DRG-based inpatient reimbursement, high-cost maternity outlier language, or any specific rule for a cesarean DRG with MCC.

General Modifier 22 policy allows increased reimbursement for eligible surgical procedures. For Louisiana Medicaid, modifier 22 is required for unusual circumstances on the most appropriate CPT code for vaginal or cesarean section delivery when the delivery method is the same for all births, with prepayment review and payment at 125% of the fee schedule or contracted rate if documentation supports use.

state_specific_rules: LA: prepayment review and 125% payment when modifier 22 is supported

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Multiple-birth cesarean deliveries are reimbursed when billed with modifier 22 and are not subject to multiple procedure reduction. State-specific exceptions apply, including a state market exemption and several Medicaid program variations.

state_specific_rules: CO: market not subject to policy

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Assistant-at-surgery reimbursement is allowed for cesarean delivery only, but payment is capped at the assistant rate for the delivery-only code and requires an appropriate assistant modifier.

reimbursement_policies.policy_title: Assistant at Surgery Services Policy, Professional
reimbursement_policies.evidence: Global cesarean section codes are not reimbursed when billed by an assistant-at-surgery. The policy only allows assistant reimbursement for the delivery-only cesarean code with an appropriate assistant modifier.

This payer reimburses cesarean delivery CPT codes when an approved ICD-10 diagnosis supports the delivery. Elective cesarean deliveries without a high-risk diagnosis are not denied, but they are paid below the allowable amount. Non-global cesarean delivery services are separately reimbursable only when the assistant surgeon requirement is met. This policy governs professional cesarean delivery claims, not DRG outlier payment methodology.

state_specific_rules: New Mexico: U1 required for 59510, 59514, 59515 when medically necessary
New York: U7, U8, or U9 required on delivery codes
Texas: U1, U2, or U3 required on delivery codes; U3 not reimbursable
provider_role_restrictions: Assistant surgeon requirement for non-global cesarean delivery codes

reimbursement_policies.evidence: This is a professional obstetrical billing policy, not a DRG outlier payment policy. Cesarean delivery is reimbursed through global OB, delivery-only, or delivery-plus-postpartum CPT coding, with limited separate payment only in defined situations such as assistant surgeon claims or increased procedural services.

recommended_action.description:
Recommendation 1: Bundle CPT '59510' on Commercial obstetrical claims when there is 'same pregnancy' or 'global obstetrical claim overlap'; allow modifier '22' only on the 'same claim line' when 'medical review supports use', limited to 'once per pregnancy' and only for 'same-delivery method' or 'combined-delivery method'. Peer: Cigna and UHC also use same-claim-line controls in Commercial obstetrical billing, and both recognize modifier 22 in OB policy..

Recommendation 2: For cesarean delivery assistant-at-surgery reimbursement, pay CPT '59514' or '59620'—and align the same rule to '59510', '59515', '59618', and '59622'—only when billed on the 'same claim line' with modifier '80', '81', '82', or 'AS'; require 'non-global delivery with assistant surgeon' / 'when global not billed', limit to '1 assistant per procedure' and 'one assistant modifier per charge', and restrict to assistant-at-surgery physician, QHP, or NPP roles, including 'teaching hospital CMS qualifications'. Peer: Cigna, Humana, and UHC require assistant modifiers 80/81/82/AS on the same claim line for cesarean delivery billing, and Humana/UHC limit payment to one assistant per procedure or charge..
